title: Radiation-enhanced and moisture-synergized wearable ionic thermoelectric generator based on adhesive ionic thermoelectric elastomer

segments.text: Ionic thermoelectric material is a promising material for the harvesting low-grade thermal energy and conversion of electrical energy.
Wearable thermoelectric generators based on ionic thermoelectric materials for heat harvesting have attracted attention.

However, constrained by the narrow body-environment thermal gradients, there are still challenges in constructing wearable ionic thermoelectric generators with compact thermal contact and large electric output in multi-environment (especially during daytime).

In this work, we develop a stretchable fabric-based ionic thermoelectric generator that integrated passive radiative cooling and synergized moisture-induced potential with thermoelectric voltage in vertical units, enabling large electric generation in multi-environment.
Adhesive ionic thermoelectric units can enable structural stability and maintain electrical connection of the generator with hierarchical architecture under mechanical deformation.
Each thermoelectric unit can achieve energy density of about 0.825 J m(-2) K-1.
The integrated fabric-based generator also exhibits a reliable electrical connection under stretched, and can form compact thermal contact with human body.

The integrated generator with only 14 thermoelectric units worn on the arm can generate high voltage output (>1.5 V) at about 20 degrees C outdoors, and can charge commercial capacitors to realize energy harvesting and conversion.

title: Polyvinyl alcohol/sodium alginate double network hydrogels design for high-performance p-type ionic thermoelectric cement-based composites

segments.text: Ionic thermoelectric cement-based composites show promise due to their high Seebeck coefficients.

However, their internal ionic complexity and the coupled thermal migration behavior between cations and anions often lead to insufficient thermoelectric performance and unstable thermoelectric voltage, hindering their further development.

To address these limitations and achieve stable and high ionic thermoelectric output, a novel cement-based composite material was developed by incorporating poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and sodium alginate (SA) hydrogels.
The hydroxyl groups within the hydrogels interact with both cations and anions, thereby increasing the entropy difference in thermal migration between them.
Meanwhile, the integrated hydrogel structure provides accelerated pathways for ion transport, synergistically enhancing the overall ionic thermoelectric effect.

Furthermore, a calcium nitrate (Ca(NO3)2) immersion treatment was applied to modify the ionic composition within the cement matrix, further optimizing the differential thermal migration entropy of cations and anions and resulting in additional improvements in thermoelectric performance.

At PVA and SA contents of 2.0 wt% and 0.5 wt%,the prepared cement-based composite exhibits exceptional ionic thermoelectric properties, with the maximum thermoelectric voltage increasing from -16.3 mV to +109.6 mV under the 45 degrees C temperature difference, achieving a transition from N-type to P-type behavior.Upon treatment with calcium nitrate (Ca(NO3)2) immersion, a thermoelectric voltage of 133.4 mV was achieved, along with a power factor (PF) of 0.62 mu Wm- 1K- 2.
To the best of our knowledge, the highest Ptype ionic thermoelectric performance reported to date for cement-based composites was achieved in this work.
This study presents a promising strategy for developing high-performance and stable cement-based ionic thermoelectric materials.

title: Ionic thermoelectric osmotic energy conversion for harvesting low-grade waste heat from electronic heat sink

segments.text: Efficient utilization of low-grade waste heat generated from electronic device is synergistically beneficial for its thermal management and power supply.
However, the existing technologies of converting waste heat below 100 degrees C into electricity in electronic device remain challenging.
Based on ion-selective transport in nanopores under a temperature gradient, osmotic energy conversion becomes a potential technique to realize efficient thermoelectric conversion.
We present an ionic thermoelectric osmotic energy conversion device for harvesting low-grade waste heat from an electronic heat sink.

When the heat flux of electronic heat sink is increased from 1000 W/m2 to 3000 W/m2, the ionic thermoelectric osmotic power density after 90 min' operation is consolidated from 11.69 mW/m2 to 77.01 mW/m2 owing to the increased temperature difference from 18.24 degrees C to 43.60 degrees C between aqueous solutions across the ion exchange membrane.
In addition, the transient ionic thermoelectric coefficient slightly oscillates around 0.5 mV/K under various heat fluxes, exhibiting a stable thermoelectric sensitivity.
Furthermore, the optimum ionic thermoelectric coefficient and power density of osmotic energy conversion is achieved at an ion concentration of 0.01 M and 0.05 M, respectively.

As the pH value of aqueous solution is increased from 3 to 11 under an electronic heat flux of 3000 W/m2, the output power density is enhanced from 46.91 mW/m2 to 83.01 mW/m2 with a stable ionic thermoelectric coefficient about 0.47 mV/K due to strengthened nanopore surface charge density.
This work offers a promising route for efficient management of waste heat from electronic heat sink to realize thermoelectric energy conversion.

title: Rational Design of Robust and Efficient Natural Leather-Based Ionic Thermoelectric Detectors for Energy-Autonomous and Anti-scalding

segments.text: Compared with those traditional initiating devices of anti-scalding systems, ionic thermoelectric sensors with energy-autonomous performance show higher reliability.

However, the current ionic thermoelectric materials (i-TEs) suffer from complex nano-/micro-channel design, high production costs, environmentally unfriendly, weak mechanical properties, as well as the low moving speed of ions.

Herein, the functional leather collagen fibers-bearing natural channels are employed as the polymer matrixes, while the trisodium citrate (SC) organic acid salt exhibits the function of cationic moving self-enhancement as the primary mobile ions for signaling.

Including numerous and suitable nano-/micro-channels together with fast-moving cations, the leather-based i-TEs (LITE), LITE-SC0.75 M, possess excellent thermoelectric properties, achieving a Seebeck coefficient of 6.23 mV/K, a figure of merit of 0.084, and an energy conversion efficiency of 2.12%.

Combined with its excellent thermal stability, mechanical performance, flexibility, durability, low cost, and outstanding capabilities for low-grade heat harvesting and thermal sensing, the LITE-SC0.75 M detector bearing long service life would show great promise in automatic anti-scalding alarm suitable for multiple scenarios and extreme environments.

Therefore, the present work aims to design an efficient, robust, and energy-autonomous leather collagen fibers-based thermoelectric detector to address the limitation of current anti-scalding alarm technology as well as drive advancements in the nano-energy and its effective conversion field.Graphical AbstractThe robust leather collagen fibers-based ionic thermoelectric (i-TEs) detectors with numerous nano-/micro-channels and fast-moving cations are successfully constructed, which demonstrate great potential for automatic anti-scalding applications in various scenarios and extreme environments
